feature: Recordings and sounds go into the Library without going onto the timeline
summary: You can fill the Library before you cut: File > Import Media (Shift Command I), the plus on the Library header, or a file dropped on the shelf puts recordings and sounds there as tiles, and nothing lands on the timeline until you drag a tile onto a track.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a screen recording; the Library can be hidden.

try.do: With the Library hidden, press Shift Command I and pick a recording or a sound.
Drag a sound from the Finder over the Library shelf and hold it there.
Let go. Check the timeline: nothing new is on it.
Drag the new tile onto the Audio track, one second in.
Click the plus on the Library header.
Choose Import Media and pick the same sound again.
Draw a marquee on a picture and press Shift Command I.

evaluate: When Import opens a hidden Library, does your eye find the new tile straight away?
Does the ring on the shelf make it plain the file is going into the Library and not onto the picture?
Is Shift Command I the key you would reach for, or would Command I (Premiere and Final Cut) be better?
Does 'Already in Library' read as helpful or as noise when you import the same file twice?
Are From Capture History and Add Selection to Library worth their rows on the plus?
rough: The tiles are still 68 points wide, so names are cut in the middle (Tutor....mp4). The mock draws them at least 96 wide, two to a row. Filed as its own task.
The mock's first step, a new empty video with nothing on it, does not exist yet, so this starts from a recording. Filed as its own task.
With a marquee up, Shift Command I stays Invert Selection, the Photoshop key. Import only takes the key when there is nothing to invert.
The mock's menu rows carry icons; these are plain macOS menu rows.
Dropping the music on Audio moved the recording's own sound down to a new Audio 2 track. That is how the timeline already treats a clip landing there, not new with this change.
A capture landing straight in the Library, the mock's third way in, is not here: a new capture opens its own window. From Capture History on the plus opens History instead.
